title: Timing-budget tests pass reliably on a busy machine
goal: Two hover-detection speed tests fail now and then when the computer is busy, each missing its time limit by under a millisecond, which makes a green test run a matter of luck. They should measure what they mean to measure without failing because of other work on the machine.
notes: Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/ElementBoundsTests.swift:268 (50 ms budget over 20 runs, saw 55.9 ms) and :535 (30 ms budget, saw 30.6 ms). Options: take the best of several batches instead of one mean, run them serialized (.serialized trait) so parallel suites do not compete, or widen the budgets with a comment. Serves measure-redline only indirectly (keeps its commits unblocked); filed under the arrow-caption epic because that is where it bit.
acceptance: readingTheNeighboursStaysInsideTheMouseMoveBudget and readingTheSubjectsCostsFourProbes pass three consecutive full Scripts/test.sh runs while another swift build is running.
The budgets still catch a real regression (a deliberately doubled probe count fails).

log.note: Reproduced first: full suite under a concurrent package build failed readingTheSubjectsCostsFourProbes in 2 of 3 runs (30.0 and 53.8 ms against 30); neighbours crept to 48 of 50 ms. Idle readings sit at 50 to 65 percent of budget, so contention has no room.

Tried best-of-N wall clock: 3 loaded passes but neighbours' fastest call hit 44.5 ms. Tried thread CPU time: fastest subjects call read 30.0 ms CPU with no descheduling, so the thread was on an efficiency core. No absolute budget can tell a slow core from extra work.

Fix: the two probe-count tests now assert a RATIO against their own probe detects run back to back on the same thread (fastest of 20 rounds, thread CPU clock); guard is ratio < 1.3. The detect test keeps an absolute budget widened 10 to 20 ms with a note. Helpers print spreads so a future flake can be told from a regression.

Verified: doubled probes in ElementBounds.swift read ratio 2.00 and 2.05, 1.5x probes read 1.51 and 1.54, all fail; core file reverted. Three consecutive full Scripts/test.sh runs under a looping swift build plus six CPU burners passed with ratios 0.92 to 1.07 while absolute times inflated up to 1.7x. Idle full run green.

Serves epic-uehjr1 (staged now) by keeping its commits from failing on a busy machine. Third timing test in the same file (detectionStaysWellInsideTheMouseMoveBudget) had the same flaw and was hardened in the same change.

ElementBoundsTests: the two probe-count timing tests now assert a ratio against their own probe detects on the same thread (guard 1.3; doubled probes read 2.0), the detect test keeps an absolute budget widened to 20 ms. Verified: 3 consecutive full Scripts/test.sh runs green under a looping swift build plus six CPU burners, doubled and 1.5x probe counts fail.
